FIRST, the deleveraging midday called 'the first real one of the week' continued and deepened: open interest fell another 2.57 percent to 2,082,796,486 USD, down 4.06 percent from morning, and funding collapsed 41.25 percent to +0.0000460535265445 - longs are paying roughly half what they paid six hours ago. THIRD, and cutting the other way, the account base got MORE crowded long as price fell: the 1H long/short ratio went 1.24 at 17:00 UTC to 1.27, 1.28, 1.30, 1.32, 1.33 and now 1.32 - the highest reading of the day, set while price was making the low. Macro leaned harder against as well: the US 10-year printed 4.85 percent, a fresh 52-WEEK HIGH set today, Brent held 101.38, and the 09 September ETF row published at MINUS 100.7 million, more than double the 08 September outflow and a second consecutive negative day. The honest synthesis is that the leverage is cleaner, the flows and rates are worse, and the crowd is still on the wrong side - which justifies a token add near the flushed low and nothing larger.

FOUR named catalysts. ONE, the 08:00 UTC funding settlement. Funding is +0.0000460535265445 and has now fallen 41.25 percent in six hours; if it prints negative or near-zero at 08:00 UTC while the account ratio is still 1.32, the remaining long book is being paid to stay and the squeeze risk flips upward - that is the constructive tail. THREE, the ETF tape. The 09 September row published at minus 100.7 million with IBIT still showing a dash - IBIT is the largest fund on the tape and its number lands overnight, so the headline outflow can widen materially before Asia opens. FOUR, rates. The 10-year set a 52-week high at 4.85 percent today; the Asian session trades that print without a US cash market to absorb it. THE PROTECTION: a resting stop at 77,620.0 is RECOMMENDED this session, and the placement is the whole point. Three consecutive sessions have now wick-pierced the stated invalidation and closed back above it - 200.2 points on 09 September morning, 135.9 points tonight - and three consecutive sessions declining the stop has paid. That record argues against a stop; the overnight gap and an unrebuilt liquidation shelf argue for one. The resolution is not to skip it but to place it BELOW the trap: 77,620.0 sits 4.6 points under the 77,624.6 structural low and 144.1 points under tonight's wick, so it survives a repeat of exactly the move that would have stopped out the last three sessions and only fills if the range genuinely breaks. Size the overnight book so that fill is survivable: the paper desk carries zero futures into the gap by design.

calibration.note: Full accounting of midday's three written levels. THE REDUCE GATE FIRED AND IT WAS RIGHT. It required a settled 1H close below 78,265.0; the 21:00 UTC candle closed 78,148.4, clearing the trigger by 116.6 points, and was CONFIRMED by 77,924.4 at 22:00 UTC, 340.6 points through. Price then made its low at 77,764.1, so a trader who reduced on the first settled close avoided a further 384.3 points of drawdown from the trigger and 980.1 points from midday's 78,744.5 report price. Price now marks 78,283.0, 18.0 points ABOVE the gate, so the re-entry is available almost exactly where the exit was - which is the best possible outcome for a reduce: it bought the flush for free. THE ADD GATE REFUSED, CORRECTLY AND BY A WIDE MARGIN. It required a settled 1H close above 78,977.5; the session high was 78,794.4 and the best settled hourly close was 78,415.7, missing by 562.1 points. It was never remotely close. THE INVALIDATION AT 77,900.0 WAS PIERCED, by 135.9 points on the wick at 22:15 UTC, with no settled close below it - the 22:00 UTC candle closed 77,924.4, surviving by 24.4 points. That is the THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION in which the stated invalidation is wick-pierced and then reclaimed on the settled close, after 200.2 points on this morning's read and the same pattern at midnight. THE DECLINED RESTING STOP AT 77,900.0 WOULD HAVE BEEN FILLED, 135.9 points above the low, and price marks 78,283.0 - so declining it was right by 383.0 points, the FOURTH consecutive session that refusal has paid. Net: one gate fired and won, one gate refused and won, one wick-pierced invalidation that held on closes, and a paper trade that worked. Midday's hedging short opened at 78,744.5 with take-profits at 78,265.0 and 78,100.0; the 77,764.1 low reached both and the ledger resolves it at the higher 78,265.0 - the first futures trade of the series to be closed by a take-profit rather than a stop. The specific thing to log is that midday's stated reason for shorting rather than buying was that 78,744.5 sat dead inside the 78,000-79,500 band blamed for six consecutive losing entries, so it expressed the read synthetically instead of improvising a seventh buy. That reasoning produced the first clean win in four sessions.
